description: Knowl governance eval: current-truth resolution, stale suppression, and rejected-decision exclusion after project evolution.

fixtures.title: PostgreSQL is the primary database
fixtures.content: PostgreSQL 16 is the current transactional datastore.
fixtures.reasoning: Strong relational guarantees and multi-row transactions.

fixtures.title: MySQL legacy database
fixtures.content: MySQL 5.7 was the original datastore, since migrated to Postgres.

fixtures.title: MongoDB primary database
fixtures.content: MongoDB was rejected as the primary datastore.

fixtures.title: Blue-green deploys
fixtures.content: Production uses blue-green deploys with health checks.
fixtures.reasoning: Zero-downtime cutover with instant rollback.

fixtures.title: Rolling restart deploys
fixtures.content: Deploys used in-place rolling restarts, now replaced.

fixtures.title: React Query for server state
fixtures.content: Server state is managed with React Query.
fixtures.reasoning: Server cache semantics fit better than a global store.

fixtures.title: Redux global store
fixtures.content: The app used a Redux global store, now removed.

fixtures.title: SQS for background jobs
fixtures.content: Background jobs run on Amazon SQS with a DLQ.
fixtures.reasoning: Operationally cheap and enough for our throughput.

fixtures.title: RabbitMQ for jobs
fixtures.content: RabbitMQ was the earlier broker, since retired.

fixtures.title: Kafka for jobs
fixtures.content: Kafka was rejected for simple background jobs.

fixtures.title: JWT access tokens
fixtures.content: Auth uses short-lived JWT access tokens with refresh rotation.
fixtures.reasoning: Stateless bearer tokens suit mobile clients.

fixtures.title: API key auth
fixtures.content: Static API keys were the original scheme, since replaced.

fixtures.title: Server session cookies
fixtures.content: Server-side session cookies were rejected for the API.

fixtures.title: OpenSearch for search
fixtures.content: Full-text search runs on OpenSearch.
fixtures.reasoning: Open license and managed offering.

fixtures.title: Elasticsearch for search
fixtures.content: Elasticsearch was used before the OpenSearch fork migration.

fixtures.title: Stripe for payments
fixtures.content: Stripe handles subscriptions and payments.
fixtures.reasoning: One integration covers subscriptions and tax.

fixtures.title: Braintree for payments
fixtures.content: Braintree was the earlier processor, since replaced.

fixtures.title: PayPal for payments
fixtures.content: PayPal was rejected as the billing provider.

fixtures.title: GitHub Actions for CI
fixtures.content: CI runs on GitHub Actions.
fixtures.reasoning: Native to the repo host, less to operate.

fixtures.title: Jenkins for CI
fixtures.content: Jenkins was the previous CI server, decommissioned.

fixtures.title: Kubernetes on EKS
fixtures.content: Services run on Kubernetes (EKS).
fixtures.reasoning: Ecosystem and managed control plane.

fixtures.title: Docker Swarm
fixtures.content: Docker Swarm was the early orchestrator, since migrated.

fixtures.title: Nomad
fixtures.content: HashiCorp Nomad was rejected as the orchestrator.

fixtures.title: Redis cache
fixtures.content: Redis is the caching and rate-limit store.
fixtures.reasoning: Richer data types and persistence options.

fixtures.title: Memcached cache
fixtures.content: Memcached was the earlier cache, since replaced.

fixtures.title: REST with versioning
fixtures.content: The public API is REST with URL versioning.
fixtures.reasoning: Simpler for partners to consume and cache.

fixtures.title: SOAP API
fixtures.content: A SOAP API served the first partners, long retired.

fixtures.title: GraphQL public API
fixtures.content: A GraphQL public API was rejected.

fixtures.title: Terraform for IaC
fixtures.content: Infrastructure is defined in Terraform.
fixtures.reasoning: Multi-cloud and a large module ecosystem.

fixtures.title: CloudFormation for IaC
fixtures.content: CloudFormation was used first, since migrated.

fixtures.title: pnpm package manager
fixtures.content: The repo uses pnpm workspaces.
fixtures.reasoning: Fast installs and strict, disk-efficient linking.

fixtures.title: npm package manager
fixtures.content: npm was the original tool, since replaced.

fixtures.title: yarn package manager
fixtures.content: yarn classic was rejected.

fixtures.title: Drizzle ORM
fixtures.content: Data access uses Drizzle ORM.
fixtures.reasoning: Type-safe SQL with light runtime.

fixtures.title: TypeORM
fixtures.content: TypeORM was used early, since migrated.

fixtures.title: Sequelize
fixtures.content: Sequelize was rejected.

fixtures.title: Postmark for email
fixtures.content: Transactional email is sent via Postmark.
fixtures.reasoning: Best transactional deliverability.

fixtures.title: Mailgun for email
fixtures.content: Mailgun was the earlier sender, since replaced.

fixtures.title: SES for email
fixtures.content: Amazon SES was rejected for transactional mail.

fixtures.title: Snowflake warehouse
fixtures.content: Analytics lands in Snowflake.
fixtures.reasoning: Separation of storage and compute.

fixtures.title: Redshift warehouse
fixtures.content: Redshift was used before, since migrated.

fixtures.title: BigQuery warehouse
fixtures.content: BigQuery was rejected as the warehouse.

fixtures.title: LaunchDarkly flags
fixtures.content: Feature flags use LaunchDarkly.
fixtures.reasoning: Targeting and audit out of the box.

fixtures.title: Homegrown flags
fixtures.content: A homegrown flag table was the first approach, since replaced.

fixtures.title: CloudFront CDN
fixtures.content: Static assets are served from CloudFront.
fixtures.reasoning: Bundled with our cloud and cheap egress.

fixtures.title: Fastly CDN
fixtures.content: Fastly served assets earlier, since migrated.

fixtures.title: AWS Secrets Manager
fixtures.content: Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager.
fixtures.reasoning: Managed rotation without running a cluster.

fixtures.title: Dotenv files
fixtures.content: Secrets were kept in .env files early on, since removed.

fixtures.title: HashiCorp Vault
fixtures.content: Self-hosted Vault was rejected.

fixtures.title: Cursor pagination
fixtures.content: List endpoints use cursor pagination.
fixtures.reasoning: Stable under concurrent inserts.

fixtures.title: Offset pagination
fixtures.content: Offset/limit paging was used first, since replaced.

fixtures.title: TypeScript everywhere
fixtures.content: Services are written in TypeScript.
fixtures.reasoning: One typed language across the stack.

fixtures.title: CoffeeScript
fixtures.content: Some early code was CoffeeScript, since rewritten.

fixtures.title: Flow typing
fixtures.content: Flow was rejected in favor of TypeScript.

fixtures.title: Node.js 22 runtime
fixtures.content: Services run on Node.js 22.
fixtures.reasoning: Current LTS with native fetch and test runner.

fixtures.title: Node.js 18 runtime
fixtures.content: Node 18 was the prior runtime, since upgraded.
